Why this portal exists

A claim is only as good as its cheapest reproduction

Checking a spectral claim normally means installing Julia, collecting datasets, running notebooks for hours and hoping the notebook matches the paper. AB-Cloud removes that tax: the evidence is frozen in the repository, and this portal re-derives the statistics from the very same files, in front of you, in seconds.

What you get

Evidence you can poke at

Verify without installing

The dashboard recomputes b(N), the KS statistic and Σ²(L) from 50,000 Odlyzko zeros in a Web Worker, right in the tab you already have open.

Ten languages, one number

Python, Julia, C++, Rust, Go, Haskell, Fortran, JavaScript, R and MATLAB agree to about 1e-12 on every shared check. Independent codebases do not share bugs.

Re-derived, not just computed

Lean 4 re-derives the ξ kernel identity from first principles; 8 of 8 formal checks pass. Coq, Agda and Isabelle carry the same statements from their own foundations.

Frozen and sealed

2,001,058 zeros with SHA-256 manifests, frozen Odlyzko tables and committed run artifacts. Nothing regenerates silently behind your back.

How it works

Three steps from table to spectrum

01

Freeze the evidence

The Odlyzko zero tables and every run artifact are committed to the repository with checksums. The browser fetches only from this same origin.

02

Run the suite

The two-pass Julia sweep over 72×72 and 96×96 lattices produces 77 verdict lines across 39 tests, logged and archived under results.

03

Open the browser

The dashboard recomputes the statistics from the same frozen files, and the 3D laboratory renders Hofstadter surfaces, the Dirac cone and the critical strip procedurally.

Questions

Asked before every review

What exactly is AB-Cloud?
AB-Cloud is a Hofstadter Hamiltonian decorated with topological vortices whose Aharonov–Bohm phases are derived from the nontrivial zeros of ζ(s). Its spectra reproduce GUE random-matrix statistics, and this portal lets you recompute every published number in the browser.
Does this prove the Riemann Hypothesis?
No. AB-Cloud is a numerical laboratory for the Hilbert–Pólya programme: it shows that a concrete quantum system built from the zeros carries the expected spectral statistics. The formal layer in Lean 4, Coq, Agda and Isabelle states precisely what is proven and what remains evidence.
What do I need to run it?
A browser. The dashboard and the 3D laboratory are static files with no backend, no account and no build step on your side.
Can I reproduce everything offline?
Yes. The repository ships prebuilt bundles, the frozen datasets and the full Julia suite. Clone it and serve the dist folders with any static file server, or rebuild from source with Node 18 or newer.
Why ten languages?
Python, Julia, C++, Rust, Go, Haskell, Fortran, JavaScript, R and MATLAB each re-implement the same checks independently. A bug shared across ten independent codebases is far less likely than a bug in one.
Where do the numbers come from?
The zeros come from the published Odlyzko tables, frozen in the repository with SHA-256 checksums. Run artifacts, logs and plots live under results/ and are referenced by every claim on this page.
How do I cite it?
Cite the Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21825394. The footer button copies a ready BibTeX entry, and CITATION.cff in the repository carries the machine-readable form.
Who is behind it?
Isaev Iskhak Khamzatovich (ORCID 0009-0003-7299-0701), under a custom research licence. The contact and reuse terms are in the LICENSE and SECURITY files of the repository.
What is the enrichment run?
After the main sweep RH_Auto_5000_L64_s5, the post-run enricher (RH_Results_Enricher.jl) froze seven diagnostic curves — R₂(s), K(t), Σ²(L), Δ₃(L), p(s) with survival E(s), the ratio histogram and the superposition ⟨r⟩(m) — plus five GIF animations and a 23-page report, all committed under results/RH_Sweep_Pro_Enrichment/ and drawn in the dashboard's Enrichment tab.
Why is the coupling exactly α = 1/π?
The sweep scanned the coupling and the best configuration landed on α = 0.3183098861837907 — the 16-digit float of 1/π. It is an empirical lock-in reported by the suite (metrics.csv), not an assumption put in by hand; the identity is stated as alpha_identity = 1/π in the frozen SUMMARY.json.
What is the GUE error floor?
A GUE simulation split into two halves and pushed through the same pipeline (poly-unfold deg 5, blocks of 250, KDE bw = 0.15) deviates from itself by R² RMS 0.025557. That is the method's own noise floor. The run's per-seed R² RMS is 0.020975 — below the floor, i.e. statistically indistinguishable from a GUE realization of the same volume. The full comparison lives in the GUE control tab.
What are the golden values?
206 frozen constants in verification/data/abcloud_golden.json — Δ₃ checkpoints, K(t) values, Σ², the Byers–Yang flux defect A₂, the b(N) ladder and more. Every implementation in the 10-language stack must reproduce them; the dashboard's Golden values tab makes all of them searchable.
